craft_notes: Sthāyin: proclamation-joy (the thesis sentence of the work). Sanskrit first: thesis (become Śiva, self becomes), naming (that is transformation), overflow (rains nectar, creature-life) → L4 sets thesis+naming line 1, overflow line 2. Rows: row 1 (need-last — 'need' closes as jīvanam closes: life as need). Rupture: colon after 'indeed' — thesis sealed, rain released. Close: end-weight on creature-need (nectar FOR someone — the rain lands). Minimal pass: 'bright nectar' (divyam as bright, singable); 'turning' for pariṇāma (turning-as-transformation, same motion). Read aloud: line 1 turns (become/becomes/turning round vowels), colon, line 2 rains (rains/bright/need falling soft). Rejected: 'transformation' flat kept? — 'turning' sings, doctrine in cite; 'all beings need' expanded — killed: every creature's need is the full measure, no more.

lines: Become Śiva, the self becomes — that is the turning indeed:
forever he rains bright nectar, every creature's need.
l4.sanskrit_cite: śivībhūto bhavatyātmā pariṇāmaḥ sa eva hi / sadā sa varṣate divyam amṛtaṃ jantujīvanam

reads_against.argmap: Become-Śiva is the self — that is transformation; and he rains divine nectar, creature-life.
c1_essence: Mind to dissolution where her resting lies; self known by the firm.
